title: Conditional Sums (SUMIF / COUNTIF)
summary: Master aggregating numbers and counting records based on custom criteria in Excel using SUMIF and COUNTIF functions.

sections.title: 1. Theory & Core Concept
sections.content:
In real-world data analysis, you rarely aggregate an entire column without criteria. For example, business leaders often ask: 'What were total sales in the East region?' or 'How many orders exceeded $500?'

The SUMIF function allows you to calculate the sum of cells in a specified range that satisfy a given criteria.
keyTakeaways: If sum_range is omitted, Excel sums the cells evaluated in range.
COUNTIF syntax: =COUNTIF(range, criteria) to count occurrences matching criteria.

sections.title: 2. Syntax & Formula Breakdown
sections.explanation:
• Range (A2:A100): The range of cells you want evaluated by criteria ('Region' column).
• Criteria ("East"): The condition that defines which cells will be added.
• Sum_Range (C2:C100): The actual cells to sum ('Revenue' column).

sections.title: 3. Real Business Use Case
sections.content:
A retail manager at an e-commerce company needs to analyze monthly sales performance across 4 regions: North, South, East, and West.
Instead of manually filtering rows or making multiple copies, she uses =SUMIF(RegionRange, "East", SalesRange) to dynamically calculate regional revenue figures for executive reporting.
sections.codeSnippet:
// Regional Revenue Summary Table Formula
=SUMIF(Data!$B$2:$B$5000, Summary!A2, Data!$E$2:$E$5000)

sections.title: 4. Interactive Practice Exercise
sections.question: Suppose column A contains Product Categories ('Electronics', 'Clothing') and column B contains Sale Amounts. What formula sums sales for 'Electronics'?
sections.explanation: =SUMIF(A2:A50, "Electronics", B2:B50) evaluates Category range A2:A50 for 'Electronics' and sums matching rows in Sales range B2:B50.
